newsitem.title: DENMARK: Printed press dominates European media awards.
newsitem.headline: Printed press dominates European media awards.

text.p: Media organisations from Belgium, Britain, Germany, Netherlands and the United States won the annual Prix Stendhal press and television awards here on Friday for excellence in reporting of European issues.
The five winners, chosen by a jury of prominent European academics, officials and business and media leaders were;
-The British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) for television documentaries.
-Business Week International, the European edition of the U.S. magazine, for reporting on welfare issues in European society.
-Rotterdams Dagblad, of the Netherlands, for European economic coverage.
-Maerkische Allgemeine of Potsdam, Germany, for regional European reporting.
-Coup d'oeil of Namur, Belgium, in the category of publications for young people.
The Stendhal prizes, established in 1990, are organised by the Geneva-based Adelphi Foundation with the backing of the European Commission and the European Parliament.
The awards were presented by Lord McGregor of Durris, chairman of the Reuters Founders Share Company, the Trustees of the international news group.

The prizes, awarded to individual journalists from the winning organisations, include media internships and two journalistic fellowships at Britain's Oxford University offered by the Reuter Foundation, Reuters' educational trust.
